function.name: path_list_to_path
function.description: This function converts a list of path nodes into a path. It counts the nodes, allocates memory for points and types, and assigns them to the path. If memory allocation fails, it frees the allocated memory and returns FALSE. Otherwise, it frees any existing points and types in the path, assigns the new points and types, updates the count and datalen of the path, and returns TRUE.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: This is the head of the list of path nodes to be converted into a path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: This is the path where the converted nodes will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the conversion was successful or not. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: flatten_bezier_add

parameters.name: jobs
parameters.description: A pointer to the list of jobs.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: A pointer to the start node of the path.

parameters.name: x2
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the second point.

parameters.name: y2

parameters.name: x3

function.name: flatten_bezier
function.description: This function flattens a bezier curve by breaking it down into smaller segments that approximate the curve. It uses a list of jobs to keep track of the segments that still need to be processed. The function continues to break down the curve until the segments are flat enough, as determined by the flatness parameter.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Pointer to the start node of the path list

parameters.name: x2
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the second control point

parameters.name: y2
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the second control point

parameters.name: x3
parameters.description: X-coordinate of the third control point

parameters.name: y3
parameters.description: Y-coordinate of the third control point

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Pointer to the end node of the path list

parameters.name: flatness
parameters.description: Parameter to determine the flatness of the curve. The smaller the value, the flatter the curve

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully flattens the bezier curve, and FALSE if it fails at any point

function.name: extend_current_figure
function.description: This function extends the current figure by adding new points to the path. It checks if the new figure starts at the same point as the last point in the path, and if so, it skips the first point. It then lengthens the path, copies the new points into the path, sets the type of the first point, and fills the rest of the types with the specified type. Finally, it sets the newfigure flag to FALSE and increments the count of points in the path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Pointer to the path to be extended

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Pointer to the array of points to be added to the path

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of points in the array

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type to be assigned to the new points

function.return_type: GpStatus, represents the status of the operation. Returns 'Ok' if the operation is successful, 'OutOfMemory' if the path cannot be lengthened

function.name: add_closed_figure
function.description: This function adds a closed figure to a path. It first checks if the count is zero, if so it returns Ok. If not, it tries to lengthen the path by the count. If it fails, it returns OutOfMemory. Then it copies the points to the path at the insert_index and sets the type of the first point to PathPointTypeStart. The rest of the types are set to the input type. It then sets newfigure to TRUE, increases the pathdata count by count and sets the last type to PathPointTypeCloseSubpath. Finally, it returns Ok.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Pointer to the path where the closed figure will be added

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Pointer to the points that define the closed figure

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of points in the closed figure

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the points in the closed figure

function.return_type: GpStatus, represents the status of the operation. It can be Ok if the operation was successful or OutOfMemory if the path could not be lengthened

function.name: GdipFlattenPath

function.name: is_integer_path
function.description: This function checks if all points in a given path have integer coordinates. It iterates over each point in the path, rounds the x and y coordinates to the nearest integer, and then checks if the original coordinates are equal to the rounded ones. If any point has non-integer coordinates, the function returns FALSE. If all points have integer coordinates, it returns TRUE.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the path that will be checked for integer coordinates.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if all points in the path have integer coordinates, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: write_path_data
function.description: This function writes path data into a structure and calculates the size of the data. It checks if the path is an integer path and writes the data accordingly. It also sets the version, count, and flags of the path header. If the data parameter is NULL, it returns the size without writing any data.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the path data to be written.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the data where the path data will be written. If this is NULL, the function will only calculate the size of the data without writing anything.

function.return_type: DWORD, represents the size of the data that would be written or has been written.
